papers.title: Composition-Driven Discovery of Multimetallic Catalysts Using Features Inspired by the Virtual Crystal Approximation
papers.abstract: Abstract Structure–activity relationships built on structure-derived descriptors are a dominant paradigm in catalyst screening. However, this structure-driven framework scales poorly to multimetallic systems, where active sites are heterogeneous, dynamically reconstruct under operating conditions, and require extensive structural enumeration and system-specific descriptor engineering. Here, we introduce a composition-driven screening strategy for multimetallic catalysts using feature construction inspired by the virtual crystal approximation. Specifically, multimetallic sites are represented as composition-weighted pseudoatoms, allowing readily available elemental properties to be converted into predictive features without explicit structural modeling. Unlike elemental fractions alone, these features encode physicochemical differences among the constituent metals. We demonstrate this approach using Prussian blue analogues (PBAs) as a compositionally tunable and reconstruction-prone validation platform for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Combining the composition-derived features with symbolic regression yields an explicit expression for ranking compositions, guiding experimental identification of four high-performance PBAs. We further evaluate this strategy across six literature data sets spanning different catalyst families and reactions, independently training a model for each. Using one of the models, we screen and experimentally validate a perovskite catalyst achieving an overpotential of 189 mV at 10 mA cm–2 in acidic OER. These results demonstrate the broad applicability of virtual crystal approximation-inspired feature construction for composition-driven screening of multimetallic catalysts.

papers.title: Dopant-Free Octahedral-Distorted Spinel Cobalt Oxide for High-Performance Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Developing efficient and stable transition-metal catalysts for acidic water oxidation requires the exploration of multiple structural regulation factors. Although foreign-element doping and morphological engineering have been widely employed, they often complicate the catalyst structure and obscure the origin of activity. Here, we demonstrate that octahedral cobalt–oxygen–octahedral cobalt bond-angle distortion is a key structural parameter correlated with the intrinsic OER activity of spinel cobalt oxides. Through in situ X-ray spectroscopic and imaging techniques, we identify that this long-overlooked Co-octahedra-distortion-induced structural regulation can effectively modulate Co-3d electronic structures and Co–O hybridization. This optimization weakens the adsorption of key oxygen intermediates and increases the propensity toward the oxide path mechanism. The resulting undoped cobalt oxide exhibits high activity in the acidic oxygen evolution reaction, achieving 2.31 V at 3 A cm–2 in a proton exchange membrane electrolyzer. This discovery provides a new perspective to reevaluate cobalt spinel oxides and establish a novel structure–activity relationship between bond angle distortion and performance.

papers.title: Edge-Selective Growth of Monodisperse PtOX on Two-Dimensional Ni(OH)2 Nanosheets
papers.abstract: Abstract Precise spatial regulation of noble-metal species is crucial for maximizing metal utilization and enabling site-specific electronic interactions. Edge sites in layered hydroxides possess distinct coordination and electronic structures, yet selectively stabilizing noble-metal species at active boundaries remains challenging. We report a photoassisted edge-selective anchoring strategy to selectively anchor highly dispersed oxidized Pt species at Ni(OH)2 nanosheet edges, forming a well-defined Ni(OH)2@PtOX edge heterointerface. Structural and spectroscopic analyses reveal edge-enriched, approximately octahedrally coordinated PtOX species stabilized by strong Pt–O–Ni coupling without perturbing the bulk lattice. In methanol oxidation, the edge-engineered catalyst exhibits higher activity, faster kinetics, and selective formate production than Ni(OH)2 and non-edge-selective Pt-loaded systems. Operando spectroscopy, electrochemical analysis, and DFT show that edge-confined PtOX promotes NiOOH formation and electronically tunes adjacent unsaturated edge-Ni sites, lowering the barrier for initial methanol activation. This work establishes two-dimensional edge engineering as a strategy for constructing functionally nonequivalent heterointerfaces.

papers.title: Denitrogenative glycosylations of glycosyl sulfonohydrazides
papers.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79707-y Despite notable progress, the development of novel and efficient glycosyl radical precursors that are readily accessible, synthetically versatile, and compatible with stereoselective coupling platforms remains an ongoing challenge. Here the authors report a nickel-catalysed stereoselective denitrogenative glycosylation of redox-neutral glycosyl sulfonohydrazides via anomeric C–N bond homolysis.

papers.title: Optical observation of ultrafast carrier separation in InGaN photocatalyst nanostructures
papers.abstract: Abstract Understanding carrier dynamics in semiconductor nanostructures is essential for optimizing their photocatalytic performance. We present direct optical evidence of ultrafast carrier separation in InGaN nanostructures used for water splitting. Two types of InGaN-based photocatalysts are studied: deepnano structures, which are a p-type InGaN micro-network, and nanowires incorporating an InGaN/GaN layered heterostructure. Here, we show that rapid lateral carrier separation in these nanostructures produces observable signatures in ultrafast spectroscopy. Using combined time-resolved photoluminescence and time-resolved differential reflectance spectroscopy, we observe photoluminescence exhibiting fast decay while differential reflection remains stable. This indicates rapid carrier separation. Studies of temperature and power-dependent photoluminescence confirm that carrier separation dominates over recombination-driven decay, and Mg doping studies reveal that stronger band bending enhances the carrier separation. The physical interpretation of the observations is supported by a numerical model including drift, diffusion, and thermal relaxation. The results provide critical insights into charge carrier dynamics in InGaN nanostructures, highlighting their potential for efficient photocatalysis.

papers.title: Accelerating high-throughput catalyst screening by direct generation of equilibrium adsorption structures
papers.abstract: Abstract The adsorption energy serves as a crucial descriptor for the large-scale screening of catalysts. Nevertheless, the limited distribution of training data for the extensively utilised machine learning interatomic potential, predominantly sourced from near-equilibrium structures, results in unreliable adsorption structures and consequent adsorption energy predictions. In this context, we present DBCata, a deep generative model that integrates a periodic Brownian-bridge framework with an equivariant graph neural network to establish a low-dimensional transition manifold between unrelaxed and DFT-relaxed structures, without requiring explicit energy or force information. Upon training, DBCata effectively generates high-fidelity adsorption geometries, achieving an interatomic distance mean absolute error of 0.035 Å on the dataset from Catalysis-Hub, which is approximately 70% lower than that of the current state-of-the-art machine learning potential models. Moreover, the corresponding DFT accuracy can be improved within 0.1 eV in 94% of instances by identifying and refining anomalous predictions through a hybrid chemical-heuristic and self-supervised outlier detection approach. We demonstrate that DBCata enables accelerated high-throughput computational screening for alloy catalysts in the oxygen reduction reaction, highlighting the potential of DBCata as a powerful tool for catalyst design and optimisation.

papers.title: Entropy-engineered polar heterogeneity enables near-decoupled polarization–strain behavior for high-density energy storage
papers.abstract: Dielectric energy-storage (ES) ceramics are central to pulsed power technologies, yet excessive polarization–strain coupling in lead-free systems induces electrostrain, compromising ES density and device reliability. Here, we introduce configurational entropy ( S config ) as a quantitative design parameter to engineer polar heterogeneity and regulate polarization–strain interactions in lead-free relaxor ferroelectrics (RFEs). Entropy engineering generates chemical heterogeneity, local lattice distortions, strain-field fluctuations, and polar fragmentation, disrupting long-range polar coherence and reducing the spatial cooperativity of polarization-induced deformation while preserving large field-induced polarization. This entropy-mediated reconstruction of the polar landscape yields an ultralow electrostrictive coefficient Q 33 of ~0.010 m 4 C –2 in a (Bi 0.5 Na 0.5 )TiO 3 -based high-entropy RFE, enabling a near-decoupled polarization–strain response with high polarization and suppressed macroscopic electrostrain. Multilayer ceramic capacitors achieve a recoverable ES density of 21.5 J cm –3 at 1200 kV cm –1 , together with a low electrostrain of 0.073% at 300 kV cm –1 . Atomic-scale imaging reveals vortex and antivortex polarization configurations associated with entropy-induced structural heterogeneity and lattice distortions. Phase-field simulations demonstrate that heterogeneous polarization states redistribute elastic energy and reduce cooperative polarization-induced deformation. This work establishes S config as a quantitative descriptor for engineering weak electromechanical coupling and high-ES-density performance in lead-free dielectric capacitors.

papers.title: A membrane-guided strategy for optimizing proton exchange membrane fuel cells via spatially controlled acid distribution
papers.abstract: Efficient regulation of phosphoric acid (PA) distribution is vital for advancing high-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells. PA migration from the membrane into the catalyst layer (CL) enhances proton accessibility but compromises membrane conductivity, highlighting the need to balance acid distribution within the membrane electrode assembly. Here, we propose a membrane-guided strategy enabling systematic evaluation of PA distribution effects and identification of a favorable acid content range. By designing side chain–grafted polybenzimidazole (PBI) membranes with abundant acid-binding sites, we achieve tunable acid doping levels and regulate PA partitioning through acid-polymer interactions. To compare PA accumulation, we introduce the mass ratio of phosphorus to platinum in the CL (PA CL /Pt CL ) as a semiquantitative descriptor of CL acid content and use distribution of relaxation times analysis to decouple its influence on ohmic resistance, oxygen reduction kinetics, and oxygen transport. We identify a favorable PA CL /Pt CL range of approximately two to three under the present conditions, while the nearly twofold enhancement over OPBI highlights coordinated control of membrane transport and the CL acid state.

papers.title: Synergistically Driven Catalytic Activity in Amorphous–Crystalline CoCe–NiMo‐Oxide Heterostructures for Efficient Ampere‐Level Water Splitting
papers.abstract: To counter the environmental issues, recently hydrogen has emerged as a substitute candidate for fossil fuels which can produce via electrolysis of the water requiring efficient electrocatalyst. In this work, we synthesized amorphous–crystalline heterostructured CoCe–NiMo composite electrocatalysts via a single‐step hydrothermal technique, and their interface‐engineered electrochemical properties are investigated. CoCe–NiMo composite electrocatalyst shows enhanced HER activity with the lowest overpotential of 129 mV at current density of 10 mA cm −2 and Tafel slope of 117 mV dec −1 . Remarkably, it achieved an industrial‐grade current density of 1000 mA cm −2 only at 486 mV, excellent operational stability, and maximum current density of 2500 mA cm −2 . The overall water splitting (OWS) activity of the electrolyzer fabricated using CoCe–NiMo at cathode (HER) and CoCe at anode (OER) obtained current density of 10 mA cm −1 only at a cell voltage of 1.66 V, whereas an industrial‐grade current density of 800 mA cm −2 is also achieved at lowest voltage of 2.28 V. Moreover, the OWS performance at elevated temperature of 55°C with 6 M KOH electrolyte was further reduced to 1.53 V and 2.33 V to achieve current density of 10 and 2000 mA cm −2 demonstrating its commercial applicability. The excellent electrochemical properties and durability at harsh condition in alkaline medium suggesting the potential of the CoCe–NiMo‐based catalyst for commercial electrolyzers.

papers.title: Tuning the Electrode Interfacial Microenvironment in Nontraditional Water Electrolysis: Insights From Direct Seawater Electrolysis
papers.abstract: Nontraditional water electrolysis offers a promising route for sustainable green hydrogen production using alternative water resources. Among these systems, direct seawater electrolysis (DSE) provides a representative platform for investigating electrode interfacial challenges, particularly chloride corrosion at the anode and insulative mineral precipitation at the cathode. Many existing studies focus on isolated component design, often struggling to bridge the critical disconnect between idealized kinetic activity and practical operational durability. Here, we introduce the interfacial microenvironment as a unifying analytical framework. By emphasizing the extreme and dynamic localized conditions at the electrode-electrolyte interface, this perspective shifts the research focus from intrinsic material properties to the precise regulation of this dynamic boundary. We first discuss the mechanisms of anodic corrosion and cathodic scaling. We then conduct a comprehensive summary of advanced strategies of both electrodes from the perspective of the microenvironment, categorizing them into physical space barriers, chemical regulation, and dynamic control. Next, cross-scale synergistic integrations are explored, highlighting complementary electrolyte engineering, asymmetric system designs, multiscale theoretical modeling and machine learning. Finally, we outline critical challenges and perspectives to guide future research toward the practical deployment of DSE and related nontraditional water electrolysis technology.

papers.title: In Situ Exsolution of Cooperative Ni‐Ru Catalytic Sites for Ammonia‐Fueled Proton‐Conducting Ceramic Fuel Cells
papers.abstract: Green ammonia (NH 3 ) is a promising carbon‐free fuel for proton‐conducting ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs). However, the sluggish NH 3 decomposition kinetics and the NH 3 ‐induced degradation of Ni‐based anode constrain the performance of NH 3 ‐fueled PCFCs. Herein, we advocate in situ exsolution strategy to construct CeO 2 ‐based catalytic layer incorporating Ni and Ru catalytic sites, which can promote NH 3 decomposition and mitigate NH 3 ‐induced anode degradation in NH 3 ‐fueled PCFCs. The synergistic interaction between Ni and Ru facilitates NH 3 conversion at intermediate temperatures, thereby reducing the direct exposure of the underlying Ni‐based anode to concentrated NH 3 . The resulting cell achieves a 43.6% enhancement in peak power density over the bare cell at 600°C and maintains stable operation for over 100 h at 650°C and 0.5 A cm −2 in dry NH 3 , with a voltage degradation rate of 0.04% h −1 . These findings demonstrate that in situ exsolution strategy offers a promising route toward efficient and durable direct ammonia‐to‐electricity conversion in intermediate‐temperature PCFCs.

papers.title: Fe‐Regulated Coupled 2e−/4e− ORR Pathway in a Conductive Co‐Fe HITP Framework for Rechargeable Zinc‐Air Batteries
papers.abstract: Zinc‐air batteries based on non‐precious‐metal catalysts are promising for sustainable energy conversion, yet their performance is hindered by sluggish oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) kinetics and limited understanding of pathway regulation in metal–organic framework (MOF)‐based catalysts. Herein, we report a bimetallic electron‐conductive Co‐Fe framework based on 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexaiminotriphenylene (HITP), in which Fe incorporation shifts the ORR toward a greater four‐electron contribution. Structural, electrochemical, and density functional theory (DFT) analyses reveal complementary dual‐site roles: Co sites favor peroxide formation via the 2e − pathway, whereas Fe sites promote O─O bond activation and subsequent reduction of peroxide intermediates. Peroxide intermediates generated on Co sites can be further converted to OH − at Fe sites. As a result, the Co 2.2 Fe 0.8 (HITP) 2 catalyst exhibits enhanced ORR activity and enables a rechargeable zinc‐air battery with an open‐circuit voltage of 1.37 V, a peak power density of 154.2 mW cm −2 , and a high specific capacity of 843 mAh g Zn −1 along with enhanced cycling stability. This work establishes electron‐conductive MOFs as a well‐defined platform for probing ORR mechanisms and highlights dual‐metal site engineering as an effective strategy for modulating ORR pathways and improving electrocatalytic performance.

papers.title: Interfacial Electronic Structure Modulation and Surface Reconstruction in (Ni, Co)Se2/MoSe2 Mott‐Schottky Heterojunction for pH‐Universal Hydrogen Evolution
papers.abstract: Achieving efficient hydrogen evolution across the entire pH range remains challenging because distinct reaction environments require fundamentally different interfacial catalytic properties. Herein, a (Ni, Co)Se 2 /MoSe 2 heterostructure was rationally constructed on carbon cloth through a hydrothermal‐selenization strategy to regulate the interfacial electronic structure and optimize hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) kinetics. Benefiting from the formation of a Mott‐Schottky heterointerface, pronounced charge redistribution and electronic coupling are achieved, leading to optimized hydrogen adsorption/desorption behavior and accelerated interfacial charge transfer. As a result, the optimized catalyst only requires overpotentials of 36, 83, and 67 mV to achieve 10 mA cm −2 in acidic, alkaline, and neutral electrolytes, respectively, together with enhanced long‐term stability over 100 h at 50 mA cm −2 under alkaline conditions. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further reveal that the heterointerface induces d‐band‐center modulation and weakens the excessive interaction with hydrogen intermediates, thereby facilitating hydrogen desorption and reducing the HER energy barrier. In addition, in situ Raman and post‐catalytic characterizations demonstrate that surface reconstruction under alkaline conditions further contributes to the dynamic evolution of catalytically active sites. This study provides a general strategy for designing high‐performance electrocatalysts capable of adapting to diverse reaction environments.

papers.title: Basal Plane Passivation of Ti3C2Tx MXenes Through Prussian Blue Analogue Nanoparticles Anchoring for Efficient and Selective Electrochemical Ammonia Synthesis
papers.abstract: Two‐dimensional (2D) MXene‐based materials have emerged as promising electrocatalysts for aqueous nitrogen fixation. However, their performance is limited by inactive basal planes, weak N 2 adsorption, and hydrophilic surface terminations that hinder N 2 binding and promote the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, we report basal‐plane activation of Ti 3 C 2 T+ MXenes via decoration with Prussian blue analogue (PBA) nanoparticles. The PBA nanoparticles mask hydrophilic surface groups, suppress HER, and enhance N 2 adsorption. Strong synergistic interactions between PBA nanoparticles and the Ti 3 C 2 T x matrix significantly boost electrocatalytic nitrogen reduction reaction (ENRR) activity, while MXenes provide mechanical robustness and chemical stability to the PBAs. The degree of basal plane activation and synergism is tuned by varying the transition metal centers in PBAs and by controlling MXene surface termination in the composites. The PBA metal centers regulate N 2 adsorption strength and stabilization of reaction intermediates, whereas MXene terminations control proton accessibility and electron transfer, collectively dictating ENRR selectivity. Owing to favorable d‐orbital interactions, FeHCF/Ti 3 C 2 T x delivers the highest NH 3 yield rate of 106 µg mg cat −1 h −1 (91 µg cm −2 h −1 ), whereas CuHCF/F‐Ti 3 C 2 achieves the highest Faradaic efficiency of 95% at ‐0.2 V.

papers.title: Laser Fabrication of Multiscale‐Structured Ru Nanocluster‐Integrated Carbon Nanotube Film Electrodes for Efficient and Durable Hydrogen Evolution
papers.abstract: Integrated hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrodes are promising for high‐current‐density anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE), yet their performance is constrained by insufficient catalyst‐support coupling and inefficient bubble transport. Herein, we develop a laser‐fabricated multiscale Ru nanocluster/carbon nanotube film integrated electrode (f‐Ru/LCNT), with the entire fabrication process requiring only minutes. A microsecond laser first constructs a three‐dimensional lamellar array architecture on carbon nanotube films, creating hydrophilic and aerophobic pathways for rapid hydrogen release. Subsequently, femtosecond‐laser irradiation drives the in situ formation of Ru nanoclusters with strong Ru–O/C interfacial bonding, thereby reinforcing electronic metal‐support interaction (EMSI) within the integrated electrode. The resulting f‐Ru/LCNT delivers excellent alkaline HER activity, requiring an overpotential of only 61 mV at 100 mA cm −2 in 1 M KOH. When employed as the cathode in an AEMWE device, the electrode enables a cell voltage of 1.83 V at 1 A cm −2 and continuous operation for 1000 h at 0.5 A cm −2 , with a low voltage degradation rate of 0.13 mV h −1 . This work provides a rapid and scalable laser preparation strategy for constructing durable integrated electrodes for practical hydrogen production.

papers.title: Breaking the Activity–Stability Trade‐Off of RuO2‐Based Electrocatalysts for Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzer: Modulation Strategies and Mechanism Elucidation
papers.abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE) is a pivotal technology for renewable green hydrogen production, yet its large‐scale deployment is limited by expensive and rare Ir‐based oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrocatalysts. RuO 2 emerges as a promising Ir‐free alternative attributed to relatively high reserves and optimal binding affinity for OER intermediates that overcomes the strong‐binding limitations of Ir‐based catalysts. However, the applications of RuO 2 in PEMWE are severely hindered by the inherent activity–stability trade‐off and severe overoxidation/leaching under harsh industrial operation. Against this background, various advanced electronic and geometric modulation approaches have been adopted to simultaneously enhance the activity and stability of RuO 2 to push forward its practical applications. In this review, we start with a comprehensive overview of the recently developed strategies for enhancing the activity and stability of RuO 2 in PEMWE. Then, the underlying mechanisms of each strategy in breaking the activity–stability trade‐off of RuO 2 ‐based electrocatalysts are systematically described. Finally, key challenges and forward‐looking optimization strategies are proposed. This review will deliver fundamental insights and rational guidelines for designing robust low‐cost RuO 2 ‐based electrocatalysts toward scalable industrial PEMWE deployment.

papers.title: Stacking‐Controlled Spontaneous Polarization in Zn–In–S Nanosheets for Efficient Piezo‐Photocatalytic H2O2 Production Toward Uranium Recovery
papers.abstract: Efficient uranium recovery from wastewater is vital for nuclear fuel sustainability and environmental protection. However, conventional photocatalytic and adsorption approaches suffer from sluggish charge separation, limited active sites, and poor selectivity. Piezo‐photocatalysis, integrating light and mechanical stimuli, can address these issues by accelerating charge dynamics, which calls for piezo‐photocatalysts with tunable polarization and well‐defined crystal configurations. Herein, ternary Zn–In–S layered nanosheets (ZnIn 2 S 4 , Zn 2 In 2 S 5 , and Zn 3 In 2 S 6 ) with tunable metal‐layer stacking configurations are fabricated via chemical vapor transport (CVT). By adjusting the Zn/In stoichiometry, we precisely govern the stacking geometry and crystal symmetry, enabling programmable spontaneous polarization and piezo‐photocatalytic activity. Among them, Zn 2 In 2 S 5 exhibits the strongest spontaneous polarization (ΔV = 3.44 eV, µ = 3.534 Debye), delivering the highest hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) production rate (689 µmol·g −1 ·h −1 ) under combined ultrasonic and light irradiation. DFT reveals that Zn 2 In 2 S 5 optimizes interfacial electron transfer to *O 2 and *OOH intermediates and lowers the free‑energy barrier for the rate‑determining *OOH formation, rationalizing its superior two‑electron oxygen reduction activity. The in‑situ generated H 2 O 2 selectively precipitates uranyl ions (UO 2 2+ ) as metastudtite ((UO 2 )O 2 ·2H 2 O), achieving an uptake capacity of 1709.3 mg·g −1 . Our findings unveil the intrinsic structure‐polarization‐catalysis correlation induced by crystal stacking and symmetry, establishing a paradigm for designing efficient piezo‐photocatalysts toward uranium recovery.

papers.title: High‑Entropy Perovskite Anodes for Efficient Water Oxidation Reaction in Protonic Ceramic Electrolysis Cells
papers.abstract: Protonic ceramic electrolysis cells (PCECs) have emerged as promising energy conversion devices due to their high efficiency and environmental friendliness. However, the development of excellent anodes with high catalytic activity of water oxidation reaction, ionic conductivity and durability remains a critical challenge. In this study, high‐entropy oxides (HEOs) of La(Co 0.4‐ x Fe 0.2 Ni 0.2 Cr 0.2 Sc x )O 3‐ δ were reported as anodes for PCECs. The effects of Sc on the phase structure, microstructure, catalytic activity, and electrochemical performance of the HEOs were systematically investigated. The HEO‐Sc3 ( x = 0.3) oxide exhibited the highest catalytic activity with an area‐specific resistance of 0.34 Ω cm −2 at 600°C, concluded by analyzing the oxygen vacancy concentration, hydrated proton concentration, and free energy of the oxygen evolution reaction. Besides, the diversification at the B‑site of perovskite and increased Sc dopant significantly reduced the thermal expansion coefficient and maintained long‑term material stability. Finally, a single cell based on the HEO‐Sc3 anode achieved a current density of 2.31 A cm −2 under 1.3 V and 600°C. This work not only highlights the pivotal function of Sc incorporation within HEO anodes, but also introduces a rational design pathway for constructing highly active and durable HEOs to the water oxidation reaction in PCECs.

papers.title: Interplay of Charge Trapping, Charge Separation, and Chemical Reactivity in Photocatalytic ZnSe‐Based Semiconductor–Metal Hybrid Nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Sustainable energy conversion technologies demand efficient, stable, and environmentally compatible photocatalysts. Here, we report heavy-metal-free ZnSe/ZnS─Au hybrid nanoparticles (HNPs) with controlled shell architecture and tunable Au-domain properties. These HNPs are designed to overcome intrinsic limitations of ZnSe-based nanomaterials, including surface oxidation, rapid electron trapping, inefficient charge extraction, and limited chemical reactivity. By correlating photocatalytic performance with structural analysis and ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy, we reveal how the synergistic effect of shell characteristics and metal-domain properties governs photocatalytic functionality. The ZnS shell (partial, thin, or thick) determines the interplay between surface passivation and charge separation, with complete and thicker shells effectively suppressing surface traps but limiting electron transfer. The Au domains, ranging from single-atom catalysts (SACs) to crystalline tips, further modulate charge separation and chemical reactivity, with larger domains enhancing electron extraction at the expense of reactivity. Optimal photocatalytic performance is achieved with a thin shell decorated with sub-nanometric clusters, enabling efficient charge separation while maintaining substantial surface passivation and high chemical reactivity. This work establishes design principles for heavy-metal-free HNPs, showing that parallel tuning of shell and metal-domain characteristics allows precise control over photocatalytic functionality, paving the way for high-performance photocatalysts in sustainable energy applications.

papers.title: In Situ Fluorescence Imaging of Electrode‐Structure‐Dependent Dissolved Oxygen Distributions During Electrocatalytic H2O2 Production
papers.abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is an important green oxidant, and its electrosynthesis via the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) provides a sustainable alternative to the conventional anthraquinone process. However, H 2 O 2 production is governed not only by catalyst properties but also by the local dissolved oxygen (DO) distribution at the electrode–electrolyte interface, which remains difficult to resolve using conventional bulk measurements. Herein, we develop an in situ fluorescence imaging system based on the oxygen‐dependent quenching of tris(2,2‐bipyridine) ruthenium(II) (Ru(bpy) 3 2+ ), enabling quantitative visualization of fluorescence‐derived DO variations in the near‐electrode region during electrocatalytic H 2 O 2 production. A reliable calibration correlates fluorescence intensity with DO concentration, while a DnCNN‐based denoising strategy suppresses fluorescence noise, improves the detection limit, and preserves pixel‐scale spatial information. Using this system, current‐dependent near‐interface fluorescence‐derived DO variation is monitored, revealing rapid initial DO redistribution followed by a quasi‐steady transport–reaction balance. Comparative studies of carbon paper and gas diffusion electrodes reveal distinct electrode‐architecture‐associated near‐interface DO responses, suggesting differences in local oxygen accessibility and interfacial transport behavior. Spatially resolved analysis of laser‐perforated porous electrodes reveals heterogeneous DO distributions in non‐pore regions, pore interiors, and pore edges. This work provides a quantitative in situ approach for probing electrode‐structure‐dependent DO distributions during H 2 O 2 electrosynthesis.

papers.title: Facilitated Zn2+ Transport and Preferential Zn (100) Deposition Enabled by Amorphous ZrOx‐C Hybrid Thin Film for High‐Performance Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Although aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) are emerging as promising candidates for large‐scale energy storage due to their intrinsic safety and cost‐effectiveness, the practical deployment of metallic zinc (Zn) anodes is still plagued by uncontrolled dendrite growth, corrosion, and competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) at the Zn/electrolyte interface. Surface/interface engineering with organic–inorganic hybrid layers has recently proven effective in homogenizing Zn 2+ flux and suppressing parasitic reactions. In parallel, ultrathin inorganic oxide coatings such as ZrO 2 have been shown to enable dendrite‐free cycling in aqueous media.​ In this study, an amorphous zirconium oxide–carbon ( a ‐ZrO x –C) hybrid thin film is engineered on the Zn anode surface via ultraviolet–ozone treatment, yielding an interphase with a dense ZrO x outer layer and an underlying Zr–O–C network. Such a gradient organic–inorganic architecture is designed to facilitate selective Zn 2+ ion transport while simultaneously blocking direct contact between Zn and the electrolyte, thereby mitigating corrosion, HER, and tip‐enhanced dendritic growth. The optimized a ‐ZrO x –C coating layer (30 nm in thickness) on the Zn anode delivers a prolonged cell lifespan of over 1200 h at 1 mA cm −2 , and the corresponding Zn||NH 4 V 4 O 10 full cell maintains a high discharge capacity of 222 mAh g −1 after 300 cycles under 0.3 A g −1 .

papers.title: Cationic Natural Scallion Membranes for Efficient Osmotic Power Generation
papers.abstract: Natural scallion membranes located on the inner wall leaf sheaths serve as inherent nanofluidic channels for the transport of soluble nutrients and ions during plant growth, thus providing a promising candidate for fabricating low‐cost, sustainable, and high‐performance ion‐selective nanofluidic membranes toward osmotic power generation. In this work, soluble cuticular lipids were first removed from the natural scallion membrane using a methanol/chloroform mixture. Negatively charged phosphate groups were then grafted onto the cellulose backbone through a urea‐assisted phosphorylation reaction. The as‐prepared phosphorylated scallion membrane exhibits a markedly improved cation selectivity and ion permeation flux. When employed for osmotic power generation, the membrane delivers a maximum output power density of 19.79 W/m 2 under a 50‐fold salinity gradient (0.5/0.01 M NaCl), which outperforms most reported biomass‐derived nanofluidic membranes. This work provides a viable and sustainable approach to fabricate high‐performance nanofluidic membranes for osmotic energy conversion using ubiquitous plant membranes in nature.

papers.title: Tailoring Zn2+ Solvation for Dendrite‐Free and High‐Efficiency Aqueous Zinc Batteries
papers.abstract: Aqueous zinc‐metal batteries (ZMBs) offer high capacity, intrinsic safety, and low cost but remain challenged by dendrite growth, hydrogen evolution, and interfacial instability. Here, we develop a solvation‐engineered hybrid electrolyte comprising 3 M Zn(OTf) 2 in water, methanol, and dimethyl sulfoxide (3:1:1, v/v/v). Methanol disrupts the hydrogen‐bond network, while DMSO stabilizes Zn 2+ coordination, collectively forming a unique solvation structure as confirmed by isothermal titration calorimetry, density functional theory, and Raman spectroscopy. This environment promotes preferential triflate anion decomposition, yielding an in situ fluorine‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that passivates zinc, reduces water activity, and suppresses hydrogen evolution. As a result, Zn||Zn cells cycle stably for over 4000 h at 0.5 mA cm −2 , Zn||Cu cells achieve 99.8% coulombic efficiency over 2000 cycles, and Zn||MnO 2 cells deliver > 150 mAh g −1 at 1C with sustained cathode stability. This work demonstrates a simple, scalable solvation‐engineering strategy that stabilizes zinc interfaces without complex additives or highly concentrated electrolytes, advancing the practical deployment of aqueous ZMBs.

papers.title: Phytochemical Molecular Engineering Reconfiguring Solvation Chemistry and Interfacial Energy for Highly Reversible and Long‐Lifespan Zn‐Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Severe hydrogen evolution, sluggish desolvation kinetics, and chaotic dendritic growth severely impede the commercialization of aqueous zinc‐ion batteries. Herein, a sustainable phytochemical molecular engineering strategy is proposed by introducing a natural chenpi extract (CPi) additive featuring multi‐component synergy. Benefiting from abundant multi‐functional bio‐molecules, CPi serves as a dual hydrogen‐bond donor/acceptor to disrupt the aggressive proton‐conduction network, fundamentally suppressing side reactions and parasitic hydrogen evolution. Concurrently, strong Zn 2+_ CPi coordination reconfigures the Zn 2+ solvation sheath, lowering the desolvation energy barrier and accelerating transmission kinetics. Furthermore, the preferential adsorption of aromatic moieties precisely modulates the interfacial energy, guiding rapid lateral ion flux and promoting the exclusive growth of the thermodynamically stable (100) texture. Consequently, this modified electrolyte empowers Zn 2+ symmetric cells with an ultra‐long lifespan exceeding 3600 h, and ensures an exceptional average Coulombic efficiency of 99.53% over 1000 cycles in Zn||Cu cells. Crucially, the practical Zn||MnO 2 full cells exhibit a remarkable capacity retention of 84.7% after 2000 cycles. This work opens a green, bio‐inspired avenue for implementing highly reversible, long‐life zinc metal anodes.
